findings.claim: mappingKey matches any continuation line of a multi-line quoted description that starts with a lowercase word followed by a colon and a space (for example `  note: see the docs` or `  when: the user asks`). That is ordinary prose, not a key. Such a description is now cut back to its first line, which is the old gentle-ai behaviour this reader was meant to improve on. The registry row loses the rest of the description and the trigger text, with no diagnostic.

generatedRow is a regular expression that decides which table lines Compose deletes. A foreign row that happens to have the shape `| `x` | ... | user | `y` |`, such as a hand-written row with scope user or project, is treated as generated and dropped on refresh. This is much narrower than before, but ownership is decided by shape alone. A line with CRLF endings would also fail the `$` anchor and be kept as foreign, so it would stay next to its regenerated copy as a duplicate.
